articles.title: Prasidh Krishna injury concern clouds India's big win vs West Indies; Kotak confirms hamstring strain
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India’s emphatic eight-wicket win over West Indies in the second ODI came with an injury concern as fast bowler Prasidh Krishna suffered a
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India’s emphatic eight-wicket win over West Indies in the second ODI came with an injury concern as fast bowler Prasidh Krishna suffered a hamstring strain and could bowl only five overs in Guwahati. India are monitoring the pacer’s condition, with scans scheduled to assess the extent of the injury on Thursday.Prasidh returned figures of 1/45 from his five overs after pulling up during his spell as West Indies posted a record 405/7. India subsequently chased down the target in just 43.3 overs to take an unassailable 2-0 lead in the three-match series.Prasidh being monitored, Dhir fineIndia batting coach Sitanshu Kotak confirmed after the match that Prasidh was dealing with a hamstring strain and would undergo further assessment."Prasidh Krishna has a strain in the hamstring, he is being monitored. They will do scans and we will have an update by tomorrow evening," Kotak said.The injury could force India to make a change for the series finale in Mullanpur on Saturday. Prasidh is not part of the squad for the five-match T20I series against West Indies beginning in Lucknow on October 6.Naman Dhir also had to leave the field after twisting his ankle while bowling 6.1 overs, but Kotak played down concerns over the all-rounder, saying the issue was related to cramps."Naman is someone who normally doesn't get cramps, but it can happen," he said.Dhir had taken on an increased bowling workload after Prasidh's curtailed spell, while India’s other bowlers struggled to contain a West Indies batting line-up that piled up 405 runs.Kotak defends Guwahati pitch after record run-festThe injury concerns came after a remarkable batting-dominated contest in which more than 800 runs were scored and five centuries were recorded, including Shubman Gill’s double hundred and Rohit Sharma’s century.With the nature of the pitch drawing criticism, Kotak said there was no such thing as a perfect surface in cricket."When we talk about pitches, see, I don't think anyone in the world can make a so-called 'perfect pitch'," Kotak said."You can never say this wicket will have 250 or 300 runs. There will always be criticism (there is a batting collapse curators will be criticised and vice-versa when it turns out to be a belter)," he said.Kotak also pointed to the changing standards of ODI batting, noting how 183 was once a formidable total in the 60-over era before modern batting has pushed expectations towards 400-plus scores."So whether it is only the wicket to blame or the standard of batting is going high, the way guys are batting, it's debatable," he said."But yes, there will be a time when we'll have difficult wickets in one-day games also, and different venues will have different wickets. So hopefully by then we should be prepared."Rohit-Gill partnership leaves Kotak impressedKotak credited India’s top order for turning what initially appeared to be a daunting chase into a routine pursuit.Rohit and Gill added 255 for the opening wicket in only 26.2 overs before Virat Kohli contributed 29 off 19 balls. Gill remained unbeaten on 223 as India reached 406/2 in 43.3 overs."It's one of the best I have seen in ODI cricket," Kotak said of the Rohit-Gill partnership."It's one of the best I have seen in ODI cricket," he said about Rohit-Shubman's 255-run opening wicket stand that came in just 26.2 overs."The way we batted -- Shubman and Rohit started, and then Kohli also contributed. By 32 overs, 320 runs, the game was more or less over."Kotak also praised Gill’s hunger to convert his century into a huge score despite the heat and humidity."I feel players have that hunger. Normally we see a batter getting out after reaching hundred. But the way Gill was playing, I knew he would get a double," Kotak said.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: India crush Sri Lanka by 124 runs, set up Asian Games gold-medal clash against Pakistan
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India produced a dominant all-round performance to crush Sri Lanka by 124 runs in the second men's cricket semifinal of the Asian Games in
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India produced a dominant all-round performance to crush Sri Lanka by 124 runs in the second men's cricket semifinal of the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya on Thursday, setting up a mouth-watering gold-medal clash against arch-rivals Pakistan on Saturday.After posting 169/7 on a turning pitch, India tore through Sri Lanka's batting line-up with a devastating new-ball burst and bowled them out for just 45 in 9.5 overs. The defending champions' bowlers never allowed Sri Lanka to settle into the chase, with Jasprit Bumrah, Axar Patel and Abhishek Sharma leading the rout.Pakistan had earlier booked their place in the final after beating Bangladesh by six wickets in the rain-truncated first semifinal.Scorecard: India vs Sri Lanka, Asian Games semifinalBumrah, Axar set up Sri Lanka collapseDefending 170, India made an explosive start as Bumrah struck twice in his opening over. A run-out in the second over added to Sri Lanka's problems, leaving them three wickets down almost immediately.Axar then tightened the screws in the fourth over, picking up two wickets to reduce Sri Lanka to 18/5. With the pitch offering considerable assistance to the spinners, the chase quickly turned into a procession.Asian Games Full Coverage | Medal Tally | ScheduleSri Lanka continued to lose wickets at regular intervals and had no answer to India's disciplined attack. Abhishek eventually completed the demolition job, taking two wickets in two balls to wrap up the innings at 45.The margin of victory underlined India's complete control of the semifinal and ensured the defending champions moved into Saturday's gold-medal match without having to face a serious challenge after the powerplay.Kishan, Sooryavanshi rescue IndiaIndia had also been tested with the bat after Sri Lanka opted to bowl first. The turning conditions made stroke-making difficult, and Sri Lanka used spin almost exclusively during the early part of the innings.Abhishek Sharma fell for seven after hitting a six, while Sanju Samson was dismissed for seven by ambidextrous spinner Tharindu Ratnayake.Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, however, provided the spark India needed. The 15-year-old smashed 38 from just 21 balls, peppering the Sri Lankan attack with trademark strokeplay before falling to Sahan Arachchige.His innings included six fours and two sixes and helped India reach 58/2 in the powerplay. But wickets continued to fall, with captain Shreyas Iyer and Axar Patel also departing as Sri Lanka's spinners kept the pressure on.It was left to Ishan Kishan to provide the finishing push. The left-hander remained unbeaten on 80 from 46 balls, attacking the spinners down the ground and finding the boundary regularly. Four of his sixes came between long-on and long-off, while he also struck four fours.Kishan's composed assault ensured India reached a competitive 169/7, a total that proved more than enough once Bumrah and the spinners got to work.Pakistan await in gold-medal clashIndia's reward for the comprehensive victory is a high-profile final against Pakistan on Saturday. The two sides will now meet with the Asian Games gold medal at stake, adding another chapter to their long-running sporting rivalry.For India, the semifinal offered a reminder of their depth across both departments. Kishan and Sooryavanshi provided the impetus with the bat, while Bumrah's early strikes and Axar's double blow ensured Sri Lanka's chase never got going.The focus now shifts to the final, where India will look to complete their campaign with gold against Pakistan.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Prasidh Krishna sustains hamstring injury, set to miss 3rd ODI against West Indies
articles.summary: MUMBAI: In a slight worry for India conjuring the busy cricket season ahead, it has emerged that fast bowler Prasidh Krishna will miss the third and final
articles.body: MUMBAI: In a slight worry for India conjuring the busy cricket season ahead, it has emerged that fast bowler Prasidh Krishna will miss the third and final ODI against West Indies, to be played at Mullanpur in Chandigarh on Saturday (October 3) due to a hamstring injury.Prasidh bowled only five overs (1-45) in India’s eight-wicket win in Guwahati before walking off the field. The Karnataka pacer has been diagnosed with a hamstring injury.Opening the attack, Prasidh bowled four overs initially. He returned for the 31st over for the second spell but it lasted for only one over and did not bowl again. Prasidh’s injury forced India to bowl part-timer Naman Dhir, who delivered 6.1 overs, although he too had earlier walked off the field due to a cramp.The Indian team is set to fly out of Guwahati on Thursday, but Prasidh will instead fly to Bengaluru and report to the BCCI's Centre of Excellence, where he will undergo treatment for his injury.Prasidh is not part of the five-match T20I series that follows the ODIs and will begin in Lucknow on Oct 6, and thus he has some time to recover. However, considering the fine form that he has been in the last few months, India would hope that Prasidh recovers from the injury well in time before their upcoming tour of New Zealand, which starts with the opening T20I on Oct 22.India batting coach Sitanshu Kotak confirmed after the match that Prasidh was dealing with a hamstring strain and would undergo further assessment."Prasidh Krishna has a strain in the hamstring, he is being monitored. They will do scans and we will have an update by tomorrow evening," Kotak said.Prasidh's absence could pave the way for Mohammed Siraj, who has been a bit controversially ‘rested’ from the first two ODIs, to play in the final ODI, though India also have the opinion of recalling allrounder Nitish Kumar Reddy, who was excluded from the second ODI.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: When is India vs Pakistan Asian Games 2026 gold medal match? Check date, time, venue
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India will face Pakistan in the men’s cricket gold medal match at the Asian Games 2026 on Saturday, October 3.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India will face Pakistan in the men’s cricket gold medal match at the Asian Games 2026 on Saturday, October 3. The much-awaited clash will be played at the Korogi Sports Park in Nisshin. The match will start at 1:30 PM local time.India booked their place in the final with a dominant 124-run win over Sri Lanka in the semi-final on Thursday. Pakistan, meanwhile, defeated Bangladesh by six wickets in their semi-final to set up a blockbuster final against India.India beat Sri Lanka in semi-finalIndia, led by Shreyas Iyer, were sent in to bat after Sri Lanka won the toss. They posted 169 for seven on a difficult pitch.Ishan Kishan played a key innings for India, scoring an unbeaten 80 off 46 balls. He hit four boundaries and five sixes.Teenage batter Vaibhav Sooryavanshi also made an impact on his return to the Indian XI. He scored 39 runs and helped India recover after the early dismissals of Abhishek Sharma and Sanju Samson.India then produced a superb bowling performance to bowl Sri Lanka out for just 45.Jasprit Bumrah struck twice in the opening over and put Sri Lanka under pressure immediately. Axar Patel, Abhishek Sharma and Washington Sundar also picked up wickets, while three Sri Lankan batters were run out.India vs Pakistan Asian Games 2026 final: All you need to knowMatch: India vs Pakistan, Men’s Cricket Gold Medal MatchDate: Saturday, October 3, 2026Time: 1:30 PM local time (10:00 AM IST)Venue: Korogi Sports Park, NisshinWhere to watch: Sony Sports NetworkIndia eye another Asian Games goldIndia are the defending champions in men’s cricket. They won the gold medal at the 2022 Asian Games in Hangzhou.Pakistan, meanwhile, will be looking for their first-ever Asian Games gold medal in men’s cricket. Their women’s team have previously won gold at the Games.The India-Pakistan final will also come after a difficult start to the men’s cricket event, with six consecutive matches abandoned because of bad weather.How Pakistan reached finalPakistan entered the final after beating Bangladesh by six wickets in the other semi-final.The match was reduced to 13 overs per side because of a delay caused by wet weather. Bangladesh scored 111 for seven before Pakistan chased down the target in 11.3 overs.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Rishabh Pant lean patch continues, falls for 10 runs against Jammu & Kashmir in Irani Cup Day 1
articles.summary: Rishabh Pant had a disappointing outing in the Irani Cup as the Rest of India captain and wicketkeeper was dismissed for just 10 runs against Jammu &
articles.body: Rishabh Pant had a disappointing outing in the Irani Cup as the Rest of India captain and wicketkeeper was dismissed for just 10 runs against Jammu & Kashmir at the Sher-i-Kashmir Stadium on Thursday.Pant, who faced 36 balls and hit one four, attempted to attack Umar Nazir but ended up slicing the ball straight to Qamran Iqbal at short cover-point. Pant stepped out of his crease and moved towards the leg side before trying to smash the delivery through the covers. However, he only managed to get a thick slice, bringing an end to his stay at the crease.Rest of India suffered another blow soon after Pant's dismissal when Saransh Jain was bowled by Sahil Lotra for 5. Lotra tossed the ball up and got it to dip and turn away, beating Jain's outside edge and crashing into the off stump.With Jain's dismissal, Rest of India slipped to 150/6 after 51 overs, having lost six wickets in the first innings. Earlier, Shikhar Mohar was the only batter to score a half-century, while Sarfaraz Khan contributed 45. Sanat Sangwan and Sudip Kumar Gharami made 1 and 8 respectively.Jammu & Kashmir, led by Paras Dogra, won the toss and opted to bowl first in the five-day Irani Cup fixture, which is being played in Srinagar from October 1 to 5.Playing XIs of Rest Of India vs Jammu & Kashmir for Irani CupJammu and Kashmir (Playing XI): Qamran Iqbal, Shubham Khajuria, Shubham Pundir, Abdul Samad, Paras Dogra(c), Kanhaiya Wadhawan(w), Sahil Lotra, Abid Mushtaq, Lone Nasir Muzaffar, Sunil Kumar, Umar Nazir MirRest of India (Playing XI): Sanat Sangwan, Sudip Kumar Gharami, Shikhar Mohan, Sarfaraz Khan, Smaran Ravichandran, Rishabh Pant(w/c), Saransh Jain, Manav Suthar, Akash Deep, Mukesh Kumar, Mukesh ChoudharyStay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Asian Games: India script history vs Sri Lanka, bowl out opposition for sub-50 total in T20Is for first time
articles.summary: India bowled Sri Lanka out for 45 in the Asian Games men's cricket semifinal in Nisshin, Japan, on Thursday.
articles.body: India bowled Sri Lanka out for 45 in the Asian Games men's cricket semifinal in Nisshin, Japan, on Thursday. The defending champions went on to win by 124 runs and set up a gold medal clash with Pakistan.Sri Lanka's 45 is also the joint-lowest T20I total by a Test-playing nation. West Indies were dismissed for the same score by England in 2019.The 45 all out was India's first time bowling an opposition side out for under 50 in T20Is. Their previous lowest total conceded was 57 for 10, scored by the United Arab Emirates in Dubai on September 10, 2025.Sri Lanka's collapse began in the powerplay, when they slipped to 31 for six while chasing India's 170-run target. Jasprit Bumrah struck twice in his opening over before Axar Patel also picked up two wickets.India needed only 9.5 overs to complete the win, with two run-outs adding to Sri Lanka's problems as the batters struggled on a turning track.Earlier, Ishan Kishan's calculated 46-ball 80 and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's 38 off 21 balls helped India post 169 for seven in 20 overs after Sri Lanka won the toss and opted to bowl."We have to perform in both batting and bowling to win. We've been waiting for some days, there was a lot of rain around. To switch on and perform like this after a long break is commendable," Axar said after the match, referring to the washed-out quarterfinal against Afghanistan and the cancellation of practice sessions due to the weather in Japan.India's win also guaranteed them a medal in the men's cricket competition. They will face arch-rivals Pakistan in the gold medal match on Saturday.Sri Lanka will play Bangladesh in the bronze medal match. Bangladesh had lost to Pakistan earlier in the day.Both the bronze medal match and the final will be played on Saturday.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
